summary:
With MLB's regular season long over, there's no today's slate to anchor on — the 14-day and 7-day windows are bone dry across all four ratings (0-0, n=0), which tells you exactly where we stand: this is the offseason lull, and the model has nothing fresh to chew on. Don't read anything into the "5L" bullpen_fatigue streak or "3W" sp streak — those are stale labels carried over from the last live stretch in-season, not anything happening now. The only recent signal at all is the 30-day strong-play window, where every rating went 3-1 (75%) for modest +1-2u, a tiny sample that shouldn't move confidence much either way.

Until games resume, lean on the season-long aggregates as your baseline for when the slate restarts. Trends remains the flagship category across all three primary ratings at 629-489 (56%, n=1118), and it's the backbone of the best combo plays: trends+sp leads all category pairings at 58% (370-268, n=638), with trends+runs right behind at 57.3% (404-301, n=705). R4's season strong-play mark of 64% (119-68, +63.0u) is the best unit-efficiency profile in the book — tightest sample but highest hit rate, worth weighting heavier once volume returns. On team trust, LAD strong plays are elite at 80% (28-7, +27.0u) and BOS strong plays sit at 76% (22-7, +19.0u) — those are the two teams to fade conservatism on when the model flags them again. NYY is the clear warning light: 49% overall and strong plays actually losing money at 39% (9-14, -4.0u), so any NYY lean needs extra scrutiny whenever the board opens back up. Bottom line for today: no action, no signal — just file away trends+sp and the LAD/BOS strong-play trust for when real games return.
